headline: 書評看富豪批判與戰後傷痕
context: 娜歐蜜克萊恩（Naomi Klein）與雅斯特泰勒（Astra Taylor）合著的新書《End Times Fascism》，分析當代激進右翼與超級富豪如何聯手，在氣候危機中趁勢崛起，並提出一套進步派的因應方法。另一本，是塞巴斯欽福克斯（Sebastian Faulks）第 17 本小說《Farewell to Eden》，講一名參與過諾曼第戰役、後來被派駐巴勒斯坦維持英國託管統治的英軍軍官，戰後仍走不出內心的陰影。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A sharp analysis of the damage wrought by the reckless super-rich, and progressive toolkit for repairing it The more power the radical rightwing nationalists of our age accrue, the greater the risk that their destructive brand of politics becomes normalised. We should not, for instance, regard it as normal that the man in charge of one of the world’s largest nuclear arsenals casually promises “a whole civilisation will die tonight”. We should not accept that history’s first trillionaire is allowed to spread racist conspiracy theories to a hitherto unimaginable extent. We should be alarmed that, here in the UK, a party tipped to lead a potential future government is trying to cruise to power in the slipstream of this international movement. In fact, we shouldn’t just be alarmed by such developments: we should stop them and urgently repair the damage already done. But how? And what is the nature of that damage? This bold, clarifying intervention from Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor provides some of the answers. “End times fascism” is their term for a convergence of interests that can broadly be understood as a response to the climate crisis. Faced with a world coming under unprecedented strain from environmental shocks and an unequal, resource-hungry economic system, today’s reactionaries are effectively saying: bring it on. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A returning British soldier is haunted by his time in Palestine in this panoramic epic set after the second world war Sebastian Faulks’s latest book focuses on the most irreconcilable geopolitical struggle of our age, the Israel-Palestine conflict. While “the sound of mortar and machine gun, the collision of flesh and metal” are integral to Faulks’s best known works, such as Birdsong, in his 17th novel the military presence is a peacekeeping one. It’s 1946 and infantry officer Philip Deval, who saw action in Normandy, is deployed to the Holy Land to take part in maintaining Britain’s mandate in Palestine. Initially Philip is second in command of a battalion overseeing febrile relationships between Jewish and Arab communities. Britain’s profound failures and manipulation in the region, and the imminence of its disastrous departure from the territory, come under scrutiny. While able to drum up motivation and cheer for the men in his battalions, privately Philip wrestles with inner melancholy. He is “shrouded” in a “loneliness … that insulates him from the world”. Experiences on the battlefield and other, slowly elucidated tragedies have led to his pessimistic bent. Much of what Philip observes in the Middle East, and his “foreboding” sense of its intractable problems, only confirms his despairing sense of human nature. It also underlines his ambivalence towards notions of divine benevolence. Continue reading...

thread_text:
娜歐蜜克萊恩與雅斯特泰勒合著的新書《End Times Fascism》，分析激進右翼與超級富豪如何聯手，在氣候危機中趁勢崛起，也提出一套進步派的因應方法。另一本，是塞巴斯欽福克斯的第 17 本小說《Farewell to Eden》，講一名參與過諾曼第戰役、戰後被派駐巴勒斯坦維持英國託管統治的軍官，始終走不出內心陰影。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 9 月 14 日發佈的報導。
threads_text:
書市這邊有兩本新書。娜歐蜜克萊恩與雅斯特泰勒合著的《End Times Fascism》，分析當代激進右翼民族主義者，如何跟超級富豪聯手，在氣候危機中趁勢崛起——書裡直言，坐擁全球最大核武庫的領袖，能輕易說出「今晚整個文明都會滅亡」這種話，本身就不該被視為正常，這本書也提出了一套進步派的因應方法。另一本，是塞巴斯欽福克斯的第 17 本小說《Farewell to Eden》，故事發生在 1946 年，主角是參與過諾曼第戰役的英軍軍官菲利普戴瓦爾，戰後被派駐巴勒斯坦，協助維持英國在當地的託管統治，眼見英國在中東的失敗與撤離，自己也始終走不出戰爭留下的孤獨與陰影。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 9 月 14 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
voice_text: 書市最近出了兩本新書。第一本《End Times Fascism》，作者是娜歐蜜克萊恩和雅斯特泰勒，分析激進右翼民族主義者，怎麼跟超級富豪聯手，在氣候危機裡趁勢崛起，也提出一套因應的辦法。另一本是塞巴斯欽福克斯的第十七本小說《Farewell to Eden》。故事發生在一九四六年，主角是打過諾曼第戰役的英軍軍官，戰後被派去巴勒斯坦，協助英國維持當地的統治。他親眼看著英國在中東一步步失敗、撤離，自己也始終走不出戰爭留下的陰影。
